stem:
Part of an electric circuit is shown in Fig. 5.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The circuit is used to produce half-wave rectification of an alternating voltage of potential difference (p.d.) *V*₍IN₎.

The output p.d. across the 14 kΩ resistor is *V*₍OUT₎.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
A component is missing from the circuit of Fig. 5.1.

Complete the circuit diagram in Fig. 5.1 by adding the circuit symbol for the missing component, correctly connected.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
A capacitor C is shown in the circuit of Fig. 5.1.

State the effect on *V*₍OUT₎ of including the capacitor in the circuit.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 5.2 shows the variation with time *t* of *V*₍IN₎.

[[fig:f2]]

Fig. 5.3 shows the variation with *t* of *V*₍OUT₎.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the time constant *τ* for the discharge of the capacitor through the resistor is 0.038 s.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the capacitance of C. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The circuit of Fig. 5.1 is modified so that it produces full-wave rectification of an input voltage.

Suggest, with a reason, how *V*₍OUT₎ now varies with time when *V*₍IN₎ is as shown in Fig. 5.2.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: A circuit diagram with a missing component in series on the upper wire, a capacitor connected across the circuit, and a 14 kΩ resistor across the output.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.2
figures.alt: A graph of input voltage against time showing a repeating square wave with positive and negative levels.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.3
figures.alt: A graph of output voltage against time showing repeated positive plateaus followed by curved decays.
